## Body

ROUND 1 - PERFORMANCE: PASS-WITH-NOTES
PR: #311
Head: 2e36d6a887a4ec4bcf251762d604a10f7f125a33
Request: 01a1fc7d-0591-73e1-a666-da8b6c35d668

No performance correctness blocker found. The added work is one daemon-wide live subscription and one serial decision per delivered lapse. There is no new timer, poll, per-seat tick, process-launch site, replay scan, or task spawned per lapse. Boot spawns one Tokio task; shutdown aborts and joins it (lib.rs:1268,374-375). Existing receiver reconciliation emits once per live-to-lapsed edge, not on every tick (delivery/mod.rs:793-805).

Cost accounting:

| Path | Actual cost and scaling |
| --- | --- |
| Subscription at rest | No timer and no SQL for unrelated events. However, subscribe_live receives/clones each broadcast Event before Subscription filters it (events/mod.rs:259-270,442-482). The extra CPU/allocation work scales with TOTAL event rate and payload bytes, not just lapse rate. One subscriber per daemon, not per seat. The broadcast ring stays bounded; this does not add an unbounded replay backlog. |
| One lapse | registry.get for one exact seat, then one process-start observation for an eligible live Copilot seat (auth_recovery.rs:560-582; registry.rs:414-423). Registry get includes the existing schema check plus its indexed seat SELECT; one API read is not one SQL statement. Claude, retired and unbound seats stop before liveness or remedy work. |
| Liveness | ProcLiveness reads proc_pidinfo on macOS or procfs on Linux. A missing PID returns without launching ps; a recycled readable PID is compared without launching ps. An existing but unreadable process, or failed local-time conversion, can use the existing single-PID /bin/ps fallback. It is absolute-path and records ps.proc-liveness-fallback before launching (proc.rs:90-104,126-175,295-305). Consequently "no launches" is the normal case, not an unconditional guarantee. |
| Inherited F212 decision | Latest recovery fact is an indexed read; a pending restart reads/decodes that seat's live controls. Composer verification performs an existing all-pane listing and one capture, normally through the persistent tmux control client. Notices read/sort the seat's holdings and resolve its projects and recipients. These scale with matching controls, panes, holdings and recipients, respectively: the COMPLETE lapse path is not strictly O(1). Sources: auth_recovery.rs:248-272,370-399,454-500; interaction.rs:522-570; tmux/src/lib.rs:484-501,896-899,1142-1151; queue.rs:800-815. |
| Remedy | One existing queued restart control, or the existing notification path. The shared monotonic 30-minute window bounds restart/notice admission, not all observation work. Actual pane control delivery and a new Copilot process can incur existing launch/initialization costs: this PR adds no launch SITE, not a promise that recovery itself creates no processes. Exceptional tmux reads also retain their existing fork fallback. No automatic revive is added. |

The lapse is a POLICY input to the existing restart decision. Exact process identity, idle, readable empty composer, and the shared window are BRAKES: removing them permits the same restart sooner or more often. The subscription's boot/lag reliability belongs to the correctness verdict; calling a missed lapse conservative does not prove successful recovery.
